title: What If the Toba Supervolcano Erupted Again?

scenes.text: What if Toba erupted again? Scientists once said it nearly wiped out humanity. Then the evidence changed.
About 74,000 years ago it blasted out at least 2,800 cubic kilometers of material, the biggest eruption in human history.
Ash fell about 15 centimeters thick across South Asia, and in places in India it piled up six meters deep.
Sulfur in the air blocked sunlight. Some estimates say global cooling of 3 to 5 degrees for years.
But sediment from East Africa shows cooling of only about half a degree, and a drought lasting under two years.
So the old claim that humans dropped to a few thousand people is not widely accepted. Toba was a giant, not the end.

description:
What if the Toba supervolcano erupted again?
It was the biggest eruption in human history, but new evidence suggests its climate effect was smaller than once believed.
